parsed.claim_reason: The family F_n={x_1,...,x_n,y_n} is pairwise intersecting (all members share x_1), yet each T_k={y_1,...,y_{k-1},x_k} is a distinct inclusion-minimal finite transversal, yielding infinitely many. So the asserted finiteness fails.
parsed.witness_reason: Every F_n is nonempty, finite, and contains x_1, so hypotheses hold. Each T_k is finite, meets F_n via y_n when n<k and via x_k when n≥k, and dropping y_i (i<k) misses F_i while dropping x_k misses F_k; the T_k are distinct, so infinitely many minimal transversals exist.
